To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the semantic analysis of a requirements elicitation document is best performed in the context of the document; (2) the semantic analysis can be performed in a generative, probabilistic framework; (3) the discourse model is more accurate than the sentence model; and (4) the accuracy of the discourse model can be further improved by incorporating additional information from the document.

1) a discourse-based model for semantic analysis of requirements outperforms a sentence-based model when the semantic representation is a live sequence chart; 2) the discourse-based model is able to handle a wide variety of semantic phenomena, including ellipsis, anaphora, and temporal and causal relations; 3) the discourse-based approach is robust and can be applied to documents with varying degrees of quality, and 4) the semantic analysis can be performed with a relatively low level of human

(i) a discourse-based model for semantic parsing is better suited than a sentence-based model to capture the semantics of requirements elicitation texts; (ii) a discourse-based approach is more robust to errors in the sentence-level parsing and semantic analysis; (iii) the discourse model can be used to improve the accuracy of the sentence-based model; and (iv) the discourse-based model is able to capture the semantics and the structure of a requirements document more faithfully than a sentencebased model.
